newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty at resistnace as dlr-selling pressure mounts.
newsitem.headline: Zloty at resistnace as dlr-selling pressure mounts.

text.p: The zloty tightened in on strong resistance at 2.5 percent from parity but currency sales caused by speculation and foreign entry into Polish T-bills may push the zloty to higher ground later on Tuesday, dealers said.
They said however that any prolonged gains above 2.5 percent from the trading band centre would likely set off a central bank currency-buying intervention.

"Currency sales are stronger today but the central bank set 2.5 percent from parity as resistance so the range is tight. If the zloty firms later today the central bank is likely to again intervene," Pawel Gajewski, forex dealer at Creditanstalt SA.

At 0805 GMT the zloty was at 2.52/2.50 percent from the parity rate, against 2.56/2.49 percent at 0710 and Monday's close at 2.51/2.49 percent. It was at 3.1655/60 to the dollar, against opening's 3.1640/60 and flat at 1.8311/16 per mark.
Dealers said that even a small central bank intervention would likely slow the zloty's upward drift on Tuesday as much of the market's currency-selling pressure was speculative.

On the money market one-day rates remained pitted at the 25-percent lombard rate as the market remained cash-strapped in the early stages of the monthly reserves as banks tried to rebuild required reserve positions, dealers said.
